questions.prompt: Name one of the four scientific instruments aboard the James Webb Space Telescope.
questions.explanation: The combined FGS/NIRISS assembly counts as one instrument. Acronyms and expanded instrument names are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

answers.label: FGS/NIRISS
aliases: Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph

questions.prompt: Name a scientific instrument that flew aboard the Spitzer Space Telescope.
questions.explanation: The complete original instrument package comprised IRAC, IRS and MIPS, including instruments used before the warm mission. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of Chandra X-ray Observatory's four main science instruments.
questions.explanation: ACIS and HRC are focal-plane instruments. HETG and LETG are the transmission-grating instruments. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

answers.label: ACIS
aliases: Advanced Charged Coupled Device Imaging Spectrometer

questions.prompt: Name one of the three human-body test mannequins carried on Artemis I in 2022.
questions.explanation: This asks for the named human-body replicas, including Commander Moonikin Campos and the two radiation phantoms. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a type of solar eclipse in NASA's four-type classification.
questions.explanation: The categories describe how the Moon covers the Sun, including a hybrid that changes between total and annular. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of Mars's three broad geological ages in its standard crater-based timescale.
questions.explanation: Use a broad age name. Early, middle and late subdivisions are accepted with their parent age. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a layer of the Sun or its atmosphere in NASA's seven-layer diagram.
questions.explanation: The diagram includes the core, two interior transport zones and four atmospheric layers, counting the transition region separately. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three main meteorite groups classified by metal and silicate content.
questions.explanation: Use a main compositional group, rather than a subgroup such as chondrite, pallasite or mesosiderite. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an astronaut who walked on the Moon during the Apollo program, 1969–1972.
questions.explanation: All twelve Apollo moonwalkers are included. Astronauts who stayed in lunar orbit are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five space agencies that partnered to assemble the International Space Station.
questions.explanation: The set consists of the five assembly partner agencies. Agency abbreviations and full English names are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four basic human tissue types.
questions.explanation: These are the broad tissue classes used in introductory histology. Specific organs and cell types are outside the set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a synovial joint type in the standard six-shape classification.
questions.explanation: The categories describe joint-surface shapes. Gliding and ellipsoid are accepted synonyms for plane and condyloid. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a bone of the adult human braincase, counting left and right versions together.
questions.explanation: Eight individual braincase bones have six names because temporal and parietal bones occur as pairs. Facial bones are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the eight carpal bones in a human wrist.
questions.explanation: This includes both carpal rows. The radius, ulna, metacarpals and finger bones are outside the set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five major white-blood-cell types in a standard differential blood count.
questions.explanation: The five broad circulating leukocyte types are counted. B and T cells both fall within lymphocytes. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four valves of the human heart.
questions.explanation: Anatomical names and common left/right atrioventricular synonyms are accepted. Generic semilunar valve is ambiguous. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three meninges surrounding the human brain and spinal cord.
questions.explanation: These are the protective membrane layers, rather than the spaces between them. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a cartilage type in the standard three-type human histology classification.
questions.explanation: The classification distinguishes hyaline cartilage, elastic cartilage and fibrocartilage by their matrix and fibers. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three principal anatomical planes used to divide the human body.
questions.explanation: The principal orthogonal planes are sagittal, frontal and transverse. Median and parasagittal describe sagittal planes. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the seven crystal systems in the IUCr classification.
questions.explanation: The IUCr system has seven crystal systems, with trigonal and hexagonal separate. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four quantum numbers used to describe an electron in an atom.
questions.explanation: Names and standard symbols n, l, ml and ms are accepted. Angular and azimuthal refer to the orbital angular-momentum number. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a direct transition between solid, liquid and gas in the conventional six-transition model.
questions.explanation: The set names each direction between the three phases. Boiling and evaporation both count as vaporization. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three permanent tissue systems of a vascular plant.
questions.explanation: This asks for the broad tissue systems, rather than individual conducting tissues such as xylem and phloem. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four living gymnosperm groups in the standard introductory classification.
questions.explanation: Group names and corresponding phylum names are accepted. Angiosperms are flowering plants and lie outside the set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three main photosynthetic carbon-fixation pathways in plants.
questions.explanation: The accepted pathway labels are C3, C4 and CAM. Expanded names for CAM and the C4 pathway are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a plant hormone group in the traditional five-group classification.
questions.explanation: The classic five groups are used here. More recently recognized signaling groups are outside this historical classification. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a main form of symbiosis in the standard three-outcome classification.
questions.explanation: The categories distinguish whether each partner benefits, is unaffected or is harmed. Predation and competition are outside this trio. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a major terrestrial biome in OpenStax Biology 2e's eight-biome classification.
questions.explanation: This specific model separates temperate forests from boreal forests and savannas from temperate grasslands. Aquatic biomes and polar ice are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five living kiwi species recognized by Save the Kiwi.
questions.explanation: Common English and Maori names are accepted. Brown kiwi by itself refers to the North Island species in this naming convention. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three adult honey-bee castes in a colony.
questions.explanation: Queens, workers and drones are the adult colony roles. Eggs, larvae and pupae are developmental stages. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element represented by a letter in the fertilizer abbreviation NPK.
questions.explanation: NPK stands for the elements nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Fertilizer label percentages may express phosphorus and potassium as oxide equivalents. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a quantity represented by one of the three standard kinds of ecological pyramid.
questions.explanation: The three kinds plot organism numbers, biomass or energy across trophic levels. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a US state whose boundary meets the Four Corners Monument.
questions.explanation: This is the single meeting point of the four state boundaries in the southwestern United States. State abbreviations are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the eight Alpine countries represented in the Alpine Convention.
questions.explanation: The convention's eight-country definition includes Monaco and Liechtenstein. The European Union is a separate contracting party. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a country crossed by the Greenwich Prime Meridian on land north of the equator.
questions.explanation: Royal Museums Greenwich lists eight countries. Antarctica is outside this northern-hemisphere set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of South Africa's three traditional national capital cities.
questions.explanation: The traditional allocation is administrative, legislative and judicial. Johannesburg houses the Constitutional Court but is outside this three-capital convention. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates.
questions.explanation: This asks for emirates, which share their names with their principal cities. Common English transliterations are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of Switzerland's four national languages.
questions.explanation: This asks for national-language status. Romansh has a more limited federal official-language role than the other three. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the eight main Hawaiian Islands.
questions.explanation: The eight-island geographic grouping includes Niihau and Kahoolawe. Big Island refers to the island of Hawaii. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a country that founded the Arab Maghreb Union in 1989.
questions.explanation: The five original member countries are used, giving this regional organization question a fixed historical scope. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the Philippines' three main island groups.
questions.explanation: The northern, central and southern island groups are intended. Individual smaller islands belong within these groups. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a lock complex of the original Panama Canal opened in 1914.
questions.explanation: The original Panamax route has three lock complexes. Agua Clara and Cocoli belong to the later expansion. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an author of The Federalist Papers, published under the name Publius.
questions.explanation: The three collaborators wrote the essays in 1787–1788. Surnames are accepted because they distinguish this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a member of the Committee of Five appointed to draft the US Declaration of Independence in 1776.
questions.explanation: The complete five-person drafting committee is included. This is smaller than the set of all Declaration signers. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an institution that owns one of the four surviving original 1215 Magna Carta manuscripts.
questions.explanation: The British Library owns two copies. Lincoln Cathedral owns the copy displayed at Lincoln Castle, and Salisbury Cathedral owns the fourth. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an Allied power that administered an occupation zone in Germany after World War II.
questions.explanation: The four postwar occupation powers are intended. These are countries rather than individual military commanders. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a state in China's Three Kingdoms period in the third century CE.
questions.explanation: The three rival states were Cao Wei, Shu Han and Eastern Wu. Their usual short names are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a member of ancient Rome's First Triumvirate.
questions.explanation: The informal alliance formed around 60 BCE joined Caesar, Pompey and Crassus. Members of the later Second Triumvirate are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three writing systems used on the Rosetta Stone.
questions.explanation: This asks for scripts. The stone uses two languages, Egyptian and Greek, written in three scripts. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a ship in Christopher Columbus's first Atlantic expedition of 1492.
questions.explanation: The three vessels were the Santa Maria, Pinta and Nina. Nina was the nickname of the Santa Clara. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three companions Dorothy meets on the road to Oz in Baum's original novel, excluding Toto.
questions.explanation: The trio seek brains, a heart and courage. Toto already accompanies Dorothy from Kansas and is excluded by the prompt. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a Christmas spirit who visits Scrooge after Marley in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
questions.explanation: The three spirits represent Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come. Marley's own ghost is excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

answers.label: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
aliases: Spirit of Christmas Yet to Come

questions.prompt: Name one of the three canticles of Dante's Divine Comedy.
questions.explanation: The three major parts describe Hell, Purgatory and Paradise. Italian titles and English translations are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five Bennet sisters in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice.
questions.explanation: First names, common nicknames and full names are accepted. Catherine Bennet is usually called Kitty. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of Mrs Rabbit's four children in Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Peter Rabbit.
questions.explanation: The original story names Peter and his three sisters. Benjamin Bunny is their cousin. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three Darling children in J. M. Barrie's Peter and Wendy.
questions.explanation: The children who fly from the Darling nursery to Neverland are Wendy and her two younger brothers. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of Fyodor Pavlovich's three acknowledged sons in The Brothers Karamazov.
questions.explanation: The acknowledged brothers are Dmitri, Ivan and Alexey. Smerdyakov's suspected parentage is outside the stated set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a member of the four-man Corresponding Society that travels in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
questions.explanation: The traveling group consists of Samuel Pickwick and his three companions. Sam Weller joins later as a servant. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a play studied in A. C. Bradley's Shakespearean Tragedy, the classic study of four great tragedies.
questions.explanation: The four plays named in Bradley's title define the set. Other Shakespeare tragedies are outside this particular study. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a house-building material used by a pig in Joseph Jacobs's version of The Three Little Pigs.
questions.explanation: Jacobs's English Fairy Tales uses straw, furze and bricks. Furze is gorse brushwood, often retold as sticks. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four basic musical texture types ending in -phony.
questions.explanation: This uses the standard monophony, homophony, polyphony and heterophony model. Adjectival forms are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an opera in Puccini's Il trittico.
questions.explanation: Il trittico comprises three one-act operas that Puccini intended to be performed together. English title translations are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a movement of Gustav Holst's original seven-movement suite The Planets, by planet name.
questions.explanation: Holst's original suite includes seven planets. Earth and the later Pluto addition by Colin Matthews are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

answers.label: Saturn
aliases: Saturn the Bringer of Old Age

questions.prompt: Name a pedal on a standard modern three-pedal grand piano.
questions.explanation: The usual grand-piano pedals are the soft, sostenuto and damper pedals. Upright practice pedals are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name the pitch of an open string on a standard four-string violin, using an English note letter.
questions.explanation: Standard violin tuning, low to high, is G3, D4, A4 and E5. Note letters with or without octave numbers are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a composer in the central three-composer group of the Second Viennese School.
questions.explanation: The central three composers are the intended group. Their surnames and full names are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an instrument in the main three-instrument wind section of a traditional gagaku ensemble.
questions.explanation: The Japan Tourism Agency identifies the hichiriki, sho and ryuteki as the three main wind instruments. Other gagaku styles can use other flutes. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three main sections of a conventional sonata-form movement.
questions.explanation: The principal sections are exposition, development and recapitulation. Optional introductions and codas are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a printmaking process family in Cornell's four-family classification.
questions.explanation: This is the four-family classification in Cornell's printmaking guide. Use a process family name. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the five basic turned-out foot positions in classical ballet, using its ordinal name.
questions.explanation: The traditional positions established by Beauchamp are first through fifth. Later parallel positions are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a complete ballet score composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky.
questions.explanation: Tchaikovsky completed three ballet scores. Later choreographies using his other concert music are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four Raphael Rooms in the Vatican Museums.
questions.explanation: English room names, their Italian equivalents and the distinguishing room subject are accepted. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

answers.label: Room of the Fire in the Borgo

questions.prompt: Name a man depicted in Rodin's six-figure monument The Burghers of Calais.
questions.explanation: The six named burghers are included. The two men surnamed de Wissant need a first name to distinguish them. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a Gaudi work included in Barcelona's original three-property UNESCO inscription in 1984.
questions.explanation: The original inscription covered Park Guell, Palau Guell and Casa Mila. Four additional works were added in 2005. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a subject among the medieval seven liberal arts.
questions.explanation: The traditional curriculum combines three language arts in the trivium and four mathematical arts in the quadrivium. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a scene shown on an interior panel of Bosch's The Garden of Earthly Delights triptych.
questions.explanation: The open triptych depicts Eden, the central Garden of Earthly Delights and Hell. The closed exterior shows the Creation. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a primitive JavaScript value type defined in ECMAScript 2024.
questions.explanation: The seven primitive types are included. Object is the remaining language type and is outside the primitive set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a position-property value defined by CSS Positioned Layout Level 3, excluding CSS-wide keywords.
questions.explanation: The property has five positioning values. Universal keywords such as inherit, initial, unset and revert are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three encoding forms defined by the Unicode Standard.
questions.explanation: The Unicode Standard defines these three encoding forms. Byte-order variants belong to their parent form. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four standardized critical chunk types in the PNG image format.
questions.explanation: Use the four-letter chunk name or expanded purpose. Private extension chunks are outside the set, and PLTE is optional in some images. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a predefined general entity in XML 1.0, using its entity name.
questions.explanation: There are five predefined entity names. Forms with an ampersand and semicolon are accepted by normalization. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a generic font family defined in CSS 2.1.
questions.explanation: CSS 2.1 defines five generic families. Later additions such as system-ui and emoji are outside this historical specification. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an HTML element that represents a group of table rows.
questions.explanation: The table model defines row groups using thead, tbody and tfoot. Individual rows and cells are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a frame type defined in HTTP/2's original RFC 7540 specification of 2015.
questions.explanation: The ten frame types defined in RFC 7540 are included. Later extension frame types are outside this historical specification. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a discipline in a standard triathlon.
questions.explanation: The three legs are swimming, cycling and running. Transition areas connect the legs and are excluded as disciplines. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an event in the women's outdoor athletics heptathlon.
questions.explanation: The seven-event outdoor program is intended. The men's indoor heptathlon has a different event list. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an official classification leader jersey at the 2022 men's Tour de France, by color or pattern.
questions.explanation: The four official classification jerseys are intended. National-champion and world-champion jerseys are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a delivery-order position on a standard four-player curling team.
questions.explanation: The four positions are lead, second, third and fourth. Skip and vice-skip are tactical roles that can be held by players in different delivery positions. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a phase of an athletics triple jump.
questions.explanation: The regulated sequence is hop, step and jump. Skip is accepted as the familiar name for the middle phase. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the nine defensive fielding positions in baseball.
questions.explanation: The designated hitter is an offensive role and is excluded. Use a specific outfield position rather than just outfielder. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a discipline combined in the sport-climbing event at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
questions.explanation: Tokyo's combined event included three disciplines. The later Paris format split speed into a separate medal event. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a sliding discipline contested on an ice track at the Winter Olympics.
questions.explanation: The three ice-track sliding disciplines are bobsleigh, luge and skeleton. Skiing and speed skating are outside this set. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a basic tea type in the six-type classification of ISO 20715:2023.
questions.explanation: The classification concerns tea from Camellia sinensis. Herbal infusions and further-processed scented teas are outside the six basic types. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a main ingredient in the traditional equal-pounds formula for pound cake.
questions.explanation: The original naming formula uses a pound each of four ingredients. Flavorings and additions in modern recipes are outside this core formula. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the three main edible parts of a whole cereal-grain kernel.
questions.explanation: The three edible parts are bran, germ and endosperm. An inedible hull or husk is excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name an ingredient in the basic four-ingredient lean yeast-bread dough.
questions.explanation: This standard lean formula contains flour, water, salt and yeast. Enrichments such as milk, sugar and fat are excluded. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a food-safety hazard category in the standard three-category HACCP model.
questions.explanation: The model categorizes hazards as biological, chemical or physical. Allergens are generally classified with chemical hazards in this model. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the eight recognized B vitamins, by number or common name.
questions.explanation: Only the eight currently recognized B vitamins are included. Historical labels such as B4 and B8 do not identify additional vitamins. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name one of the four spices in McCormick's classic Pumpkin Pie Spice blend, as described in its 2026 history.
questions.explanation: McCormick's historical blend has four named spices. Other homemade pumpkin-spice recipes may additionally contain cloves. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.

questions.prompt: Name a French tart dough in the classic three-shortcrust grouping.
questions.explanation: The classic trio consists of brisee, sucree and sablee. Puff pastry and choux belong to different pastry families. Rarity tiers are editorial estimates of familiarity.
